about: THE CARDS OF NORTHUMBRIA AND THE IRISH SEA (region northumbria_irish_sea: Eoforwic, Lindisfarena, Bebbanburg, Gyrwe, Streonaeshalch, Legacaestir, Hi, Duiblinn). Written 7 Oct 2026 by the region's weaver from the eight places files (Data/places/<port>.json), the dossiers (Design/content/dossiers) and the spine (Design/content/spine.json). A draft in the game's own files, for the user to overwrite. Each card names its port with port.id in its 'when' and is listed in its site's 'do' in the places file; the people are the places files' people, named by id in each card's note. The words are in Data/writing/northumbria_irish_sea.json under northumbria_irish_sea.<port>.<card>.<slot>: lines by their slot, an option's label under do_<key>, what comes of it under out_<key> (out_<key>_success and out_<key>_failure where there is a chance), and a picture line for each card as art.<card id>. The spine's thread flags (yk_, lf_, bk_, hy_, bs_, en_, rd_, ms_, db_) are set only for the step they name; flags the places files already named are kept as they were (gy_, st_, hi_protected, bebbanburg_, duiblinn_, legacaestir_); this file's own flags begin nis_. Grand rewards are unlock_ flags (Design/content/CHAINS.md). Lines that run between ports: the blood-price (Eoforwic, Gyrwe, Lindisfarena, Bebbanburg), the three leaves (Lindisfarena, Gyrwe, Streonaeshalch, Bebbanburg), the boys' names (Eoforwic, Lindisfarena, Bebbanburg, Hi), the abbess's question (Streonaeshalch, Lindisfarena), the lead (Eoforwic, Legacaestir), the leaf of Bede (Legacaestir, Gyrwe), the grain (Eoforwic, Bebbanburg, Gyrwe, Lindisfarena), the king's death (Eoforwic, Bebbanburg, Lindisfarena), Muirenn's word (Bebbanburg, Hi), the chest for Kells (Hi, Duiblinn), the reeve's nephew (Duiblinn, Bebbanburg), the old king (Duiblinn, Hi), the giant's kin (Eoforwic, Duiblinn, Hi) and the jet (Streonaeshalch, Eoforwic, Duiblinn, and one card at Dorestad for the count's errand). (?) in a note marks what is not attested.

cards.note: Eoforwic, the strand at the Foss mouth: Ecgwulf (eoforwic.ecgwulf, cast.ecgwulf) comes down whenever a Frisian hull is seen. The spine's thread york_blood, hook for Eoforwic: the hull looked at twice, asked whose she is (sets yk_named), and trade only through an English host; the story eoforwic.the_year_the_frisians_ran, beat 1. The killing and the flight of the Frisians are Altfrid, Vita Liudgeri I.11 (about 773); Ecgwulf, his brother's name Ecgric and every word are invented.

cards.note: Eoforwic, the book room: the scribe Torhthelm (eoforwic.torhthelm) has a letter of Alcuin's on the quarrel of King Charles and King Offa. The spine's thread black_stones, hook for Eoforwic: Alcuin was here in 790-793 and wrote of the quarrel; whether Northumbrian ships were barred too is not known (?). The sentence is our own rendering of Alcuin to Colcu, 790 (MGH Epistolae IV no. 7): the passage of ships forbidden to merchants on both sides. The story eoforwic.quarrel_in_a_letter, beat 1; the copied line is of use to the lead man at Legacaestir (harbour.forty_pigs.legacaestir). bs_ban_heard is not set here: a scribe does not enforce the ban.

cards.note: Eoforwic, the well in the waste ground, spring 796: a rumour that is TRUE. King Æthelred was killed on 18 April 796; Osbald was king for twenty-seven days; Eardwulf was made king on 14 May and hallowed at York, at Saint Paul's altar, on 26 May (Symeon, Historia regum 796; Anglo-Saxon Chronicle; chronicle_793.json 796-04-18-aethelred-killed, 796-05-14-eardwulf-king). That Osbald had burned an ealdorman in his house is the annal for 780 (?). The women are invented. The word can be carried north (harbour.gate_and_ring.bebbanburg; harbour.guest_who_cannot_stay.lindisfarena).

cards.note: Bebbanburg, the cleft gate: the thegn Cuthgar (bebbanburg.cuthgar) had the watch on 8 June 793 and saw the sails. The spine's thread holy_island, hook for Bebbanburg: the king's men saw the sails from the rock and did not come; a thegn is angry or ashamed. The story bebbanburg.sails_from_the_rock, beats 1, 5 and 8: he gives his arm-ring toward a ransom (flag bebbanburg_ring_given) or is told to spend it on a beacon (flag nis_beacon_counsel), and when word comes that a boy lives he gives the gate's word and the shield riddle (riddle_exeter_05_shield, riddles_793.json; unlock bebbanburg.gate_word). What the fortress did that day is not recorded; he and the forty men are invented. Also hears the word of the king's death (harbour.talk_at_the_well.eoforwic) and of Osbald (harbour.guest_who_cannot_stay.lindisfarena).

cards.note: Bebbanburg, the well in the rock: a rumour that is NOT true. In the first summers after the raid every sail past the outer islands is three long ships, and the vill drives its stock inland. Invented, on the fear the sources show (Alcuin's letters of 793; the raid of 794 on the Tyne); nothing came to the rock itself in these years that any source records. The steward sells in a fright; the fisherman Bacga (bebbanburg.bacga) knows better and is not believed. The women at the well saw the smoke first (the story bebbanburg.sails_from_the_rock, beat 2).

cards.note: Gyrwe, the writing house: the scribe Torhtred (gyrwe.scribe). Four stories meet at his desk. He reckons Bede's history in calves and sets the merchant to fetch skins (sets bk_knows_worth and gy_book_ordered: thread book_road, hook for Gyrwe; the story gyrwe.masters_book, beat 1); he sells a copy of the second storm leaf, riddle_exeter_02_storm_sea (10 d: thread riddle_road; gyrwe.second_leaf, beat 1) and, when it is answered, hands over the true leaf to go home to Lindisfarena (flag gy_true_leaf); and he was a boy at York's school the year the Frisians ran (sets gy_york_witness: thread york_blood, hook for Gyrwe; gyrwe.tall_frisian, beat 2). The demand for Bede's books: Boniface and Lul's letters; Liudger's leaving: Altfrid, Vita Liudgeri I.11-12. The leaf's words paraphrase Exeter riddle 2 (Thorpe 1842). He and the theft are invented.

cards.intention: Carts of stone and lime go past the Lady's hall all day to the wall. Inside, a woman with lime dust on her shoes asks short questions. On the Wirral shore, a day down the river, a tired sea-lord buys hides, and asks lightly how high the south wall stands these days.

options.label: Count the ships for the Lady, and carry her word to the Irish
Sell hides on the shore, and tell her nothing she can use

Stay out of the river until it is over

cards.note: Hi, the guest house inside the bank, on a fast day: the guest-master Óengus (hi.oengus) washes the stranger's feet and breaks the fast for him. A fast-day card. The washing of feet and the fast broken for a guest are Adomnan, Vita Columbae I.4 and I.20 (Reeves 1874, as the dossier has them); Wednesdays and Fridays as fasts among the Irish: spine calendar. The stranger from over the sea as a 'grey dog' with no standing in law: peoples/irish_gaelic.md. A cask given for the Mass makes the house's guest (flag nis_hi_guest: unlock hi.guest_bed). Aquitaine wine 45 d, sealskins 15 d the bundle (goods_793.json). He is invented.
cards.when: moored and port.id = hi and fast and year < 807
cards.title: Feet first
cards.intention: Just inside the gap in the great bank a brother stands with his sleeves rolled, beside a wooden tub. He is going to wash your feet whether you like it or not. Behind him the smell of meat is coming out of a house where, by the day, there should be none.

options.label: Eat what is set before a guest
Say you will keep the fast with the house
Give a cask of wine for the Mass
Give them the year's news to write down

memory.eat: ate what a guest is given on a fast day
memory.fast: kept the fast with the house

cards.note: Hi, the knoll of the writing hut: Abbot Bresal (hi.bresal, cast.bresal; died 801, Annals of Ulster). Lindisfarne was founded from Hi, and the two houses pray for each other's dead by name: the story hi.mothers_prayer, beats 1 and 3. Higbald's second list (flag nis_list_for_hi, from harbour.bishop_counts.lindisfarena) earns the abbot's protection (flag hi_protected: unlock hi.abbots_protection; the thread holy_island). Muirenn's cheese and her word from Bebbanburg (flag nis_muirenn_word, from harbour.grave_in_the_sand.bebbanburg) are answered (flag nis_bresal_blessing). Columba's last blessing of the island: Adomnan, Vita Columbae III.23, in our own rendering. Hi took the Roman Easter in 716 (Bede V.22). His words are invented.
cards.when: moored and port.id = hi and year < 802
cards.title: Names for the altar
cards.intention: On a knoll of bare rock facing the church stands a small hut of planks with its door open to the Sound. A very old man sits in it, with a book satchel on a peg behind him. He asks what you know before he asks what you carry.

options.label: Give the bishop's list into his own hand
Tell him what you saw on the English shore
Give him Muirenn's cheese, and her word
Ask what Columba foretold of the island

memory.shore: told what he saw on the English shore
memory.cheese: brought Muirenn's word from the rock

cards.note: Hi, the writing house: the scribe Muiredach (hi.muiredach). The spine's thread book_road, hook for Hi: the great gospel book in the making (the Book of Kells, begun on Hi about 800 as many hold (?); some 340 calfskins; no lapis in it: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Book_of_Kells). The story hi.great_gospel, beats 1 and 2: he reckons the book (sets bk_knows_worth) and gives the standing order for colours (sets bk_parchment; unlock hi.scribes_order). He also gives the margin verse 'Bitter is the wind tonight' (texts_793.json irish_viking_terror, Kuno Meyer 1911; unlock hi.bitter_wind): the verse is of about 850, in a St Gall grammar, and is given here early by the places file's leave (?). Pigments 48 d the pouch (goods_793.json). He is invented.
cards.when: moored and port.id = hi and year < 832
cards.title: The book of the four beasts
cards.intention: On the widest board in the writing house lies a calfskin leaf with one great letter on it and nothing else, full of beasts biting each other. At the next board a long stooped scribe breathes on his fingers, and looks at your bundle.

options.label: Hear him reckon the great book
Take the writing house's order stick
Ask for the verse about the wind
Look at the great letter, and touch nothing

memory.order: took the order stick for colours
memory.verse: asked for the verse about the wind

cards.note: Hi, 806 to 814: after sixty-eight of the community were killed (Annals of Ulster 806) Abbot Cellach (hi.cellach, cast.cellach) builds a new house at Kells in Ireland (807, finished 814) and the things of the island that burn must cross the sea. A passenger card: the chest with the unfinished gospel book and two brothers go to the black pool on the Liffey (flag nis_kells_chest; landed in harbour.chest_on_the_strand.duiblinn). The thread book_road, hook for Hi ('after 806 the question of carrying it to Ireland in a boat'); the stories hi.great_gospel, beat 4, and duiblinn.columbas_freight, beat 1. That the great book crossed in a merchant's keel is invented.

brother.note: one of the two brothers who go with the chest; invented

cards.title: A chest for Kells
cards.intention: There are sixty-eight new graves in a row in Oran's ground. In the church the abbot shows you a chest of oak lined with waxed hide. In it, in loose gatherings, lies the great book, a third of its pages still bare.

Say you are bound the other way

cards.note: Hi in the week of Colum Cille's feast (9 June), when boats come from every house of his family: the feast is the island's own and not one of the engine's, so the card is tied to the month. An oath card and a passenger card: under the abbot's word a stranger may make a bargain with sureties (peoples/irish_gaelic.md), sworn at the high crosses; and a pilgrim from the Dee wants passage home (the places file's tie between hi.domnall and legacaestir.osfrith, 'met at the feast of Colum Cille'). The ferryman is hi.domnall to 826 and the keepers of the boats after. Otter 40 d the bundle (goods_793.json). The seller and the pilgrim are invented.

cards.title: Colum Cille's feast
cards.intention: It is the week of the saint's feast, and boats from every house of his family lie bottom up above the weed line. Before the church door, under the tall crosses, bargains are being sworn that would hold nowhere else. Here a stranger may bargain, for the saint stands surety.

Carry the pilgrim home to the Dee
Keep the feast, and trade nothing

memory.swear: swore a bargain at the high cross

cards.note: Hi, the western plain, from 795: a brother who has sailed to the islands of the northern ocean gives the riddle of the thing that came along the wave, riddle_exeter_33_iceberg (riddles_793.json: 'a monk who has sailed north'), and from 825 a copy of what Dicuil wrote of those voyages (texts_793.json dicuil: clerics who told him, thirty years before 825, of an island where the midsummer night is light and the frozen sea lies a day's sail north; the islands since left empty 'on account of the Northern robbers'). The crane from Ireland cared for three days is Adomnan, Vita Columbae I.48 (told, not quoted). The riddle's words paraphrase Exeter riddle 33 (Thorpe 1842). A riddle card and a text card; the brother is invented.

Watch for the crane with him

cards.note: Hi, the seals' islet and the Sound: the lay boatman Domnall (hi.domnall). The seals are the house's own herd, taken by count; the seal thief of Colonsay who hid under his boat and was sent home with sheep is Adomnan, Vita Columbae I.33 (told, not quoted). After the burning of 802 timber is towed from the lochs behind the boats (the work hi.work.timber_roof); helping earns his marks for the Sound and the Torran rocks (flag unlock_pilot_torran, a grand reward: unlock hi.sound_marks). A known guest (flag nis_hi_guest) has skins at the house's reckoning (unlock hi.seal_share). Bay salt 3 d, sealskins 15 d (goods_793.json).
cards.when: moored and port.id = hi and year < 827

options.label: Give two sacks of salt for sealskins
Tow timber with him for the burned house

cards.note: Hi, the summer of 825: word comes of a fleet in the islands. Blathmac son of Flann, a king's son who chose this house because it was dangerous, has the shrine of Colum Cille buried under turf, tells the brothers who are afraid that they may go without shame, and is killed for not saying where it lies (Annals of Ulster 825; Walafrid Strabo's verses on Blathmac, of the same years, from which his words here are freely rendered). The story hi.under_the_turf and its three endings; carrying the brothers sets ms_carried_priest (thread cross_and_grove) and the abbot's protection (hi_protected). The ferryman is hi.domnall. That a merchant lay on the sand is invented.

cards.title: Under the turf
cards.intention: Word has come from Tiree of long ships working south. The shrine of Colum Cille is on the island this summer. A king's son who chose this house because it was dangerous has had it buried under turf, and after the night office he speaks to the brothers. Then he turns to you.

options.label: Take the brothers who choose to go, to Ireland
Hide the boat on the west side, and watch

cards.note: Hi, Oran's ground, from 905: the last question of the giant's kin, r-vafth-34, is kept on the island by whichever baptised Northman is tending a grave there (riddles_793.json: 'found: a Norse-Gael of the Isles', set ymirs_kin): the Norse-born brother hi.monk in the early years, and from about 995 Kali, Olvir's son (hi.kali, whose rune-cut stone for his brother Fugl is real (?)). The spine's thread riddle_road, hook for Duiblinn ('among the Norse halls of Dublin and York and at Hi'); the stories hi.giants_bones, beat 2, and duiblinn.giants_line, beat 6. He will not riddle on holy ground. The question is our own wording of Vafthruthnismal 34 (Bellows 1923: texts_793.json t-vafth-34); the answer is a boat. The hoard by the Ribble is the riddle set's own reward (rw_hoard_cuerdale), not given here.

options.label: Go down to the sand at evening for the last question
Tell him you have all the answers, and ask what shore they make
Help him clear the grass from the stone

memory.question: took the last question on the sand
memory.shore: asked what shore the answers make

cards.note: Hi, 980 to 981: Amlaíb Cuarán (duiblinn.amlaib_cuaran, historical), forty years a king at Dublin and twice at York, comes to the island a penitent after the battle of Tara and dies there (Annals of Tigernach 980; Annals of Ulster 980; chronicle_793.json 980-tara). He is brought by the merchant from the long stone at Dublin (harbour.old_kings_passage.duiblinn, flag duiblinn_old_king_aboard). The stories hi.old_kings_pennies, beat 2, and duiblinn.open_gate, beat 5: weighing his gift truly sets duiblinn_old_king_carried and wins the house no toll at Dublin while his son Sitriuc lives (flag unlock_charter_duiblinn: unlock duiblinn.kings_peace). The abbot is Mugrón (hi.mugron, historical: coarb of Colum Cille, died 980 (?)). The bag of pennies, and that a house which never struck a coin needed a merchant to weigh it, are invented.
cards.when: moored and port.id = hi and flag.duiblinn_old_king_aboard and not flag.duiblinn_old_king_carried and year >= 980 and year < 982
cards.title: The old king's pennies
cards.intention: The abbot meets the boat on the white sand. The old king walks up to the church without looking back at the sea. Afterwards, in the guest house, a bag of some hundreds of English pennies is held out to you as a man holds a live eel.

options.label: Weigh the bag truly, and say it in cows
Weigh it a little light, and keep the difference

memory.weigh: weighed the old king's gift truly
memory.light: weighed the old king's gift light

cards.note: Duiblinn before the ship-fort: the guest-house at the gate of the church by the black pool, and its keeper Tipraite (duiblinn.tipraite, to 815; his successors to 841). There is no market and no coin: a stranger from over the sea is a 'grey dog' with no standing until a man of standing makes him his guest, and a bargain needs sureties (peoples/irish_gaelic.md, after the Irish law tracts). A gift of wine and first choice of the cargo makes the guest (flag duiblinn_guest: unlock duiblinn.guest_of_the_church). No abbot is named here after Siadal (died 790, Annals of Ulster (?)); Rechru burned in 795 (AU 795.3). Wine of Aquitaine 45 d, hides 15 d (goods_793.json). He is invented.
cards.when: moored and port.id = duiblinn and year < 841

cards.title: A grey dog

options.label: Give him a cask of wine, and first choice of the cargo
Give salt, and trade through his sureties this once

cards.note: Duiblinn, the black pool, 806 to 815: the chest from Hi is landed (flag nis_kells_chest, from harbour.chest_for_kells.hi) where men of Kells wait with a cart. The stories duiblinn.columbas_freight, beats 2 to 5, and hi.great_gospel, beat 5, and their endings: carried whole (sets bk_carried: thread book_road; the abbot's protection hi_protected), or one painted leaf let go to the king of Brega's man (sets bk_lost; the deed dug_church_ground is the nearest there is to sacrilege). Óengus of Tallaght (duiblinn.oengus) asks, once, to look inside (flag duiblinn_chest_opened). Kells was given to Columba's community in 804 and the new house built from 807 (Annals of Ulster). Wax 40 d, cloth 18 d (goods_793.json). The landing here, the envoy and the sick child are invented.

cards.note: Duiblinn, Máel Ruain's house at Tallaght, a morning's walk from the pool: Óengus son of Óengoba, the Culdee (duiblinn.oengus, historical), who made a calendar of the saints in verse about 800. That he questioned a merchant for saints' days is the places file's invention (unlock duiblinn.saints_days: sets bk_parchment). The days the merchant gives are real: Willibrord on 7 November, Martin on 11 November, Boniface on 5 June, and Lambert, bishop of Maastricht, on 17 September, said by feasts as a man of 793 would say them. No ale at Tallaght: The Monastery of Tallaght 6 (Gwynn and Purton 1911). A text-wanted card: he reads a leaf out of the merchant's chest. Parchment 60 d (goods_793.json).

cards.title: A day with no saint in it
cards.intention: A morning's walk toward the hills there is a tight bank, a small church, and cells in rows, everything swept. In the writing hut a lean monk rules lines on calfskin by the light of the door, and counts something on his fingers when he sees you.

The ford of hurdles (Áth Cliath) and the shifting bar: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Dublin_to_795. The women taken at Howth: Annals of Ulster 821. He is invented.

cards.note: Duiblinn, the landing at the long stone, from 917: the king's man takes the king's share by weight. Tested jet sells here at half as much again as at York (flag st_knows_jet: the story streonaeshalch.black_and_bright, beat 4); marten skins are cheaper than anywhere a Frisian knows (the story legacaestir.farers_pennies, beat 2). The house that carried the old king pays nothing while Sitriuc lives, to 1036 (flag unlock_charter_duiblinn, from harbour.old_kings_pennies.hi). Jet 24 d, marten 120 d (goods_793.json). cards.note: Duiblinn, 980 to 981: after the battle of Tara the king of Tara shuts the town in for three days, every Irish slave in it walks out free, and old King Amlaíb Cuarán (duiblinn.amlaib_cuaran, historical) gives up the kingship and goes to Columba's island to die a penitent (Annals of Tigernach 980; Annals of Ulster 980; chronicle_793.json 980-tara). He was king at York about 941 to 944 and 949 to 952 and was not at Tara himself. That he went in a merchant's boat, the ring and his words are invented.

cards.intention: After the battle at Tara the town is full of men settling debts. An old man with the marks of rings on his wrists, and two silent servants behind him, asks the price of a passage to Colum Cille's island. He pays it without haggling, for the first time in his life.

Carry him, and take nothing
Say your boat is bound for the Dee

cards.note: Duiblinn, the law mound, from about 950: a lawsuit card. The assembly mound of the town (the Thingmote, levelled in 1685) stood south of the river outside the bank (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thingmote (?)); its date is not known, and 950 is the places file's. A case is said aloud twice so that none can claim not to have heard, and a stranger answers with sworn men beside him: the places file's custom, after the common Norse and Irish practice (?). After 980 the Irish king's Sunday rule is cried here. The skipper, the lawman and the anchor are invented. Deeds won_case and lost_case.

cards.title: The law mound
cards.intention: South of the river stands a steep green mound with a ring of posts on its flat top. On a law day the free men of the town stand round its foot. Today a Dublin skipper stands on its side and says your boat's name aloud, twice, so that none can claim not to have heard.

options.label: Answer him on the mound, with two sworn men
Pay him the worth of his anchor (12 d)
Offer him your spare anchor stone and a day's work

cards.note: Duiblinn, the ale-house by the ford road, 958 to 1001: Affraic (duiblinn.affraic), of an Irish mother and a Norse father, who counts herself descended from the ferrymen of the hurdles. A hire card. If the house once paid for the hurdles (flag unlock_pilot_liffey, from harbour.hurdles_and_bar.duiblinn, six or seven lives earlier) she knows the story: the game's thread of a house remembered. The freeing of the slaves after Tara, 980, and the ounce of gold on every plot each Christmas night from 989: Annals of Tigernach, by realms/irish_sea.md. She is invented.

cards.title: The ale-house by the ford road
cards.intention: Just inside the west gate, where the road from the ford comes in, a wattle house larger than its neighbours has a bush tied over the door. Inside are one hearth, two benches, a vat, and a woman with keys at her belt who is already telling you to shut the door.

options.label: Hire the hand she names (8 d)
Tell her it was your house that paid for the hurdles
Drink, and settle the old cups (2 d)
Sit, and listen to who is hiring for which ship

cards.note: Duiblinn, the yard on the strand, 1028 to 1064: the wright Asgrimr (duiblinn.asgrimr). A commission card. The great ship laid about 1042, thirty paces on the keel and sixty oars, is Skuldelev 2, built in the Dublin area of Irish oak (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skuldelev_ships). He trades seasoned knees for iron with the wright on the Ouse (eoforwic.shipwright), by word of mouth through skippers: the places files' tie. Hauling the house's boat for him to look under is the unlock duiblinn.wrights_strake. Rivets 16 d the keg (goods_793.json). He is invented.

cards.title: Sixty oars
